goal: Inspect this glass bottle for defects. Single static image from a fixed camera: no other viewpoints or lighting exist.

findings.description: Top-down view of a brown glass bottle mouth. At the upper right of the finish (about 2 o'clock), a step or overlapping edge in the rim is visible, with a small dark round dot just below it near the outer rim at about 3 o'clock.
hypotheses: normal thread start or mold seam on the finish
small bubble or inclusion in the glass

findings.description: The bore interior differs from the reference. The reference bore is uniformly dark, while this image shows a brown/amber lit disc with a blurry grey central region and a small dark spot. A faint light streak sits near the spot.
hypotheses: different lighting or transmission through the bottle body, showing the bottle base or interior
normal variation in how the bore is lit
foreign object or residue inside the bottle
bottle base seen through the bore

proposed=insufficient_evidence, sufficient=False. PROC-GB-004 is the procedure for static top-view images and requires comparison with the approved reference. The reference has not been fetched, so the rim step at 2 o'clock and the dark dot at 3 o'clock cannot be classified as a broken rim, contamination, or normal features (thread start, seam). The observation itself lists these as high-uncertainty with normal hypotheses. The image is not too blurred or dark, so this is a request for the reference, not a final insufficient-evidence verdict. PROC-GB-002 requires multiple lights and raking light, so it does not apply; PUB-003 is general lighting guidance and not applicable to a fixed-light image.

Lighting and pose changes are unavailable (no other poses or lights exist), so get_reference is the only available discriminating step. Observation obs_01 is not too blurred or dark to judge, so the next step is the reference comparison. | expects: If the step at about 2 o'clock and the dark dot at about 3 o'clock are normal finish features (thread start, mold seam, or reflection), the approved reference should show the same step/seam and a similar dot or none at the same location, so the observed features match. If they are a rim defect (chip or interruption) or contamination, the reference will show a smooth continuous rim and a clean interior at those positions, so the discrepancy is confirmed. Rim texture differences from the reference would also point to surface wear or residue rather than normal matte finish.
